stories.title: Nepal flash floods: MEA sets up round-the-clock control room in Delhi

As the death toll from Nepal's devastating flash floods surged to 359 on Thursday, rescuers launched a race against time to trace hundreds still missing, including 288 Indian nationals. “We have set up a control room in the Ministry of External Affairs here, which will function round-the-clock. Details of the helpline and the control room telephone numbers are being put out on our X handle, and you should be getting them soon. Our embassies, both in Kathmandu and in Beijing, have also set up 24x7 helplines,” ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said at a media briefing here. Later, the MEA shared details of the control room in a statement. “The control room can be contacted at +91 11 2308 8718 +91 11 2308 8719. For WhatsApp calls/messages: +91 9968291988. Email: situationroom@mea.gov.in,” it said. The emergency contact numbers of the Indian embassy in Kathmandu are (also on WhatsApp): +977 985 131 6807; +977 970 910 7500; and +977 981 032 6117. The massive flash floods originating in Tibet swept through central Nepal on Wednesday, devastating several towns and villages, washing away critical bridges and crippling a dozen hydropower projects, affecting multiple districts. India on Thursday said it stands “shoulder-to-shoulder” with Nepal to help it deal with the crisis as rescue operations gathered momentum in the Himalayan nation. According to the MEA, Nepali authorities can be contacted at the following helpline numbers: Tourist Police: +977 9851289445; Nepal Army: +977 9851072914 (email: dgmi-foreign@nepalarmy.mil.np); NDRRMA: +977 9851320269 /+977 9849281097; Rasuwa Police: +977 9851254960; Assistant chief district officer, Rasuwa: +977 9851164422; Nuwakot Police: +977 9851282380; Assistant chief district officer, Nuwakot: +977 9851248777; Dhading Police: +977 9851229860; Chief district officer, Dhading: +977 9851247777; Chitwan Police: +977 9855013999; Assistant chief district officer, Chitwan: +977 9855088891.

Devastating visuals from Betrawati Bazaar show homes and businesses being swallowed by the raging waters, while the swollen Narayani River has also reached danger levels.
Rescue operations are underway, with Nepal Army and private helicopters evacuating stranded people.
Here are the latest visuals of the catastrophic floods and devastation in Nepal.
A massive ice and rock avalanche triggered a sudden surge in the Bhote Koshi River, unleashing devastating floods across several districts of Nepal.
Villages were washed away, roads ripped apart and bridges swallowed by raging waters.
The destruction spread downstream into Nuwakot, where homes and shops were swept away.
Further south, the swollen Narayani River reached dangerous levels in Chitwan, with powerful waves battering the riverbanks.
From Rasuwa to Nuwakot and Chitwan, the floods have left behind widespread devastation and a devastating human toll.
More than 150 bodies have reportedly been recovered, while hundreds remain missing, including Indian pilgrims and tourists.
Nepal Army personnel have rescued nearly 200 people, including those trapped inside a hydropower tunnel.
Although floodwaters have begun to recede, the humanitarian crisis continues, with rescuers searching for survivors and families waiting for news of their loved ones.
Nepal now faces a long and difficult road to recovery.

stories.headline: India, China open door to clarifying LAC perceptions
stories.title: India, China open door to clarifying LAC perceptions
stories.summary: An eight-point outcome document released on Wednesday says the two sides ‘discussed ways to improve understanding of LAC in appropriate areas, for better border management’
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: India and China discussed ways to improve their understanding of each other’s perception of the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in the 25th Round of Special Representatives talks on the boundary question held in Beijing on Tuesday (August 25, 2026).
Indian and Chinese officials see differing perceptions of the LAC in some areas as a key factor behind tensions in both Western and Eastern Sectors.

The eight-point outcome document released on Wednesday (August 26), a day after the talks between National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and China’s Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Beijing, acknowledged those concerns.
It said the two sides “discussed ways to improve understanding of LAC in appropriate areas, for better border management”.

The joint consensus statement noted both sides agreed that “any situation on the ground would be addressed promptly through existing diplomatic and military channels, including the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination (WMCC), local commander‑level meetings and other agreed mechanisms, to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC.”
Another key outcome said an Expert Group on Boundary Delimitation would “advance discussions on an Early and Substantial Harvest of boundary delimitation”.
That process, which would start with both sides agreeing to the terms of reference, is expected to focus on sectors where there are no pronounced differences in alignment.
India has long pitched for clarifying the LAC to reduce the likelihood of incidents between patrols in areas where claims overlap.

The 1996 agreement on confidence-building measures noted the need for the two sides “arriving at a common understanding of the alignment of the LAC” and said both “agree to speed up the process of clarification and confirmation of the LAC”.
Both sides then agreed to exchange maps indicating their respective perceptions of the entire alignment of the LAC.

To that end, maps were exchanged in the Middle Sector a few years later, but the process ran aground when it came to the Western Sector in light of sharp divergences, and was subsequently abandoned in Western and Eastern sectors.
During his first visit to China as Prime Minister in 2015, Narendra Modi made a public pitch to resume the LAC clarification process.

stories.headline: One Nation, One Election: 70% back simultaneous polls, MOTN survey shows
stories.title: One Nation, One Election: 70% back simultaneous polls, MOTN survey shows
stories.summary: One Nation, One Election: 70% back simultaneous polls, MOTN survey shows
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The August 2026 Mood of the Nation survey shows 70.4% of Indians support simultaneous Lok Sabha and state assembly elections, down from 74% in January.
The findings come amid a political debate over the Modi government's.
One Nation, One Election proposal, with Congress opposing the move and the government-backed panel saying 2029 implementation is possible.
A majority of Indians continue to support the idea of simultaneous elections to the Lok Sabha and state assemblies, according to the India Today Mood of the Nation (MOTN) survey for August 2026.
However, support for “One Nation, One Election” has dipped from the previous survey.

According to the August 2026 MOTN survey, 70.4% of respondents said they support the idea of holding Lok Sabha and state assembly elections simultaneously, compared with 74% in January 2026 and 65.2% in August 2025.
Meanwhile, 24.1% said they do not support the proposal, up from 20.1% in January 2026 and 23.4% in August 2025.
The Mood of the Nation is a bi-annual survey that's been commissioned by the India Today Group for around two decades now.
The August 2026 edition was conducted by CVoter with a sample of 25,184 people directly surveyed between July 1 and August 25.
Another set of 91,795 interviews conducted over the last six months as part of CVoter's regular tracking were also used to formulate the findings of the August Mood of the Nation 2026.
The findings come amid a renewed political debate over the feasibility of implementing the Modi government's “One Nation, One Election” proposal in 2029.

Senior Congress leader P Chidambaram has asserted that simultaneous elections cannot be held in 2029 and warned that the Congress and other Opposition parties would launch a nationwide campaign against the proposed legislation, calling it a “Constitutional monstrosity” in a parliamentary democracy.

stories.headline: Supreme Court to hear plea against cash donations under Rs 2,000 to parties
stories.title: Supreme Court to hear plea against cash donations under Rs 2,000 to parties
stories.summary: Supreme Court to hear plea against cash donations under Rs 2,000 to parties
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The Supreme Court will hear a plea challenging the law allowing parties to receive cash donations below Rs 2,000.
The petition says the rule shields donor identities and weakens voters' right to informed choices.
The Supreme Court is scheduled to hear on August 31 a plea challenging the validity of a provision of the Income Tax Act that allows political parties to receive cash donations below Rs 2,000.
According to the apex court's cause list for August 31, the matter will be heard by a bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta.

The petition says the lack of transparency in political funding undermines the purity of the election process by denying voters crucial information about the source of funding, including donors and their motives.
It says this prevents voters from making a rational, intelligent and fully informed decision while casting their vote.
On November 24 last year, the top court had agreed to hear the petition and sought responses from the Centre and others.

Filed by Khem Singh Bhati, the plea has sought to strike down Clause (d) of Section 13A of the Income Tax Act, 1961, as unconstitutional, and has also referred to the apex court's 2024 judgement that scrapped the electoral bonds scheme.
Section 13A of the Act deals with the special provision relating to the incomes of political parties.

The plea said Section 13A was introduced in the Act and that income of a political party received by way of interest on securities, income from house property or income from other sources, and any income by way of voluntary contributions, are exempted from the computation of total income.

"The petitioner is seeking direction that the political parties must disclose the name and all other particulars of the person paying any amount of money to it, and no amount can be received in cash so as to maintain transparency in the political funding," the plea said.

It has also sought a direction to the Election Commission to make it a condition for registration of a political party and allotment of an election symbol that no amount can be received in cash by any political party.

stories.title: Amit Shah says Gujarat stayed drought-free after PM Modi's water push
stories.summary: Amit Shah says Gujarat stayed drought-free after PM Modi's water push

article_sentences: Home Minister Amit Shah inaugurated a 21-acre lake in Amreli and said Gujarat's water landscape changed after 2001.
He claimed sustained conservation efforts under Prime Minister Narendra Modi helped the state avoid drought-like distress.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Thursday said Gujarat had seen a major shift in water management after Narendra Modi became chief minister in 2001, and claimed the state had not faced a drought-like situation in the last 25 years.
He said this year too, despite concerns over the El Nino effect, the kind of distress seen during the droughts of the 1980s had not returned.
Shah was speaking after inaugurating a 21-acre lake developed by a trust run by diamond businessman and Padma Shri awardee Savjibhai Dholakia at Dudhala village in Amreli district.
He said water conservation measures taken over the years had improved groundwater levels, expanded farming and increased green cover across Gujarat.
Recalling the droughts of 1985, 1986 and 1987, Shah alleged there was widespread corruption under the then Congress government, including in the government-run Rafaleshwar cattle camp.
“If we create a system to save every single drop of rain and ensure it seeps into the earth, the threat of drought will never loom over our country and state.
During that drought, the Congress government was in power, and major scandals, like the Rafaleshwar scam, took place,” he said.
He also spoke about the hardship people faced at the time.

article_sentences: India defeated Germany 3-1 in the 5/6th classification match at the FIH Women’s Hockey World Cup 2026 on Thursday.
This was the team’s second-best finish ever at a World Cup.
The Salima Tete-led Indian team had narrowly missed out on a semifinal spot after failing to beat Australia in its final second-round match.

stories.headline: Kotak Mahindra Investments names Hiren Vora CFO as Siddarth Gandotra steps down
stories.title: Kotak Mahindra Investments names Hiren Vora CFO as Siddarth Gandotra steps down
stories.summary: Hiren Vora will take over as chief financial officer from September 1, following Siddarth Gandotra’s resignation at the end of August.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'steps down' in title weight 40
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: Kotak Mahindra Investments Ltd.
has appointed Hiren Vora as its chief financial officer and key managerial personnel, effective September 1, 2026, following the resignation of Siddarth Gandotra.
The company’s board, at a meeting Thursday, noted Gandotra’s resignation as CFO and key managerial personnel, effective at the close of business on August 31.
The board subsequently approved Vora’s appointment from the following day.
Gandotra will continue in his role through August 31 before Vora takes charge, ensuring an immediate transition in the company’s finance leadership.
Kotak Mahindra Investments disclosed the changes under the Securities and Exchange Board of India’s listing regulations.
Details relating to Gandotra and Vora were included in annexures accompanying the regulatory filing.
